mainTopic: Feeding animals on שבת: effort over food, the new משנה's feeding rules, responsibility for an animal's food, and adding water to bran
overview: The amud opens by finishing two challenges to רב יהודה, who holds that one may not go to effort over food that is already edible (לא טרחינן באוכלא). Each time, the גמרא answers that the food in the source was not yet edible for that animal: elephant meat or meat for puppies, rotten straw, and alfalfa for young donkeys. Next comes a new משנה listing which ways of feeding animals are allowed on שבת. The גמרא explains אובסין as stuffing a camel until its belly becomes a trough. רב יהודה and רב חסדא then disagree about the difference between המראה and הלעטה. רב יוסף challenges רב יהודה, who answers that one may feed only animals whose food is your responsibility, like a dog but not a pig. This leads to teachings about ה׳'s care for the poorly fed dog, and to a ברייתא supporting רב יהודה. Finally, the גמרא shows that the משנה's rule about putting water into bran follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה, and it begins asking who the 'יש אומרים' are in a dispute about kneading קלי. רב חסדא's answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Cutting pumpkins and a carcass seems to refute רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lets one cut pumpkins for animals and a נבלה for dogs. If the pumpkins are soft like a carcass, this means we may go to effort over food that is already edible. That contradicts רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One may cut] pumpkins before an animal and a carcass before dogs. Doesn't this mean the pumpkins are like the carcass? Just as a carcass is soft, the pumpkins are soft too. So we may go to effort with food, and this refutes רב יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a source and uses it to attack רב יהודה's rule that we do not go to effort over food that is already edible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack works by comparing the two items in the list. A נבלה is normally soft and already edible, so the pumpkins must be soft too. That means cutting is allowed even when the animal could already eat the food, which goes against רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal carcass that died without proper slaughter
we go to effort with (already edible) food

steps.confusionAlert: This step starts in the middle of a quote. The words 'one may cut' (מחתכין) came at the end of the previous amud, so 'pumpkins before the animal' is still part of that quoted source.

phrases.english: [One may cut] the pumpkins before the animal
phrases.notes: Continuation of the source quoted at the end of the previous amud

phrases.english: and the carcass before the dogs.
Is it not that the pumpkins are similar to the carcass:
just as a carcass is soft,
so too the pumpkins are soft,
so apparently we go to effort with food,
and this is a refutation of Rav Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun at the end of the previous amud
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule that one does not go to effort over food that is already edible
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Comparing the pumpkins to the soft נבלה shows that cutting edible food is allowed.

steps.title: רב יהודה reverses the comparison: the carcass is hard like the pumpkins
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that we should read the comparison the other way. The pumpkins are hard, so the נבלה must also be hard, meaning it is not yet edible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה would answer you: No. The carcass is like the pumpkins. Just as the pumpkins are hard, the carcass is hard too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יהודה by flipping the comparison. The ברייתא is about hard, inedible items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the נבלה sets the standard. רב יהודה makes the pumpkins set the standard instead. Pumpkins are normally hard, so both items need cutting to become edible. Cutting them turns non-food into food, which רב יהודה allows.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda would say to you: No,
the carcass is similar to the pumpkins:
just as the pumpkins are hard,
so too the carcass is hard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case (reversing which item defines the other)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pumpkins are soft like a carcass, so the food was already edible.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both items are hard and inedible, so cutting them is making non-food into food, which is permitted.

steps.title: When is a carcass too hard to eat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a carcass could ever be so hard that dogs cannot eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether רב יהודה's answer is realistic. Dogs usually eat meat easily. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An answer only holds up if the case it describes really exists. Here the גמרא asks for a real example of a hard carcass.

keyTerms.meaning: how can you find it (in reality)?

phrases.english: And how can you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Probes the realism of the answer in step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A realistic case of a carcass too hard for dogs to eat

steps.title: Elephant meat, or ordinary meat given to puppies
steps.stepSummary: Two cases are given. The first is elephant meat, which is very tough. The second is regular meat given to small puppies, who cannot eat it unless it is cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: With elephant meat. Alternatively, with small puppies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two real cases where a carcass is not edible until it is cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer makes the meat itself hard. The second keeps the meat ordinary, but the eaters are too young to manage it. Either way the food is not yet edible for these animals, so רב יהודה's rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יהודה, cutting is allowed only when it turns something inedible into food. The source about pumpkins and a נבלה is read to fit that rule.

phrases.english: With elephant meat.
Alternatively, with small puppies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Elephant meat, or regular meat for small puppies

steps.title: Crumbling straw and alfalfa seems to show effort with food is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן מנהרדעא taught that one may crumble straw and alfalfa and mix them on שבת. This seems to prove again that we may go to effort over food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב חנן of נהרדעא taught that one may crumble straw and alfalfa and mix them. So apparently we may go to effort with food!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source to challenge רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Straw and alfalfa are normal animal food. If one may crumble and mix them, that looks like effort over food that is already edible. That is exactly what רב יהודה forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (introduces a source as proof)

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַב חָנָן מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav Chanan of Neharde'a taught:
One may crumble straw and alfalfa and mix them.
Apparently we go to effort with food!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַב חָנָן מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new source raising the same challenge as step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule against going to effort over edible food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Straw and alfalfa are edible fodder, yet crumbling them is allowed.

steps.title: Rotten straw, and alfalfa for young donkeys
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The straw is rotten and needs preparing before it can be eaten. The alfalfa is for young donkeys, who can only eat it in small pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: The straw is rotten straw. The alfalfa is for young donkeys.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by showing that both items are not yet edible for the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same method as before is used. Each item is shown to be not-yet-food in its situation. Crumbling it therefore makes it edible, which רב יהודה allows.
steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges to רב יהודה are answered the same way: the food in the case was not yet edible for that animal.

phrases.english: The straw is with rotten straw,
the alfalfa is with young donkeys.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely by redefining both cases
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the straw and alfalfa were already edible, but they were not edible for that animal.

steps.title: משנה: force-feeding camels, calves, and chickens; mixing bran
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה forbids overfeeding or force-feeding a camel but allows placing food in its mouth. It forbids feeding calves in the manner of המראה but allows הלעטה. It allows force-feeding chickens, and it allows adding water to bran but not kneading it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not overfeed a camel and may not force-feed it, but one may put food in its mouth. One may not feed calves in the manner of המראה, but one may feed them in the manner of הלעטה. One may force-feed chickens. One may put water into bran, but one may not knead it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists which ways of feeding animals are allowed on שבת and which are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heavy, forceful feeding is too much טרחא, but gently placing food in the mouth is allowed. Adding water to bran is permitted. Kneading it into a dough is forbidden because it resembles the מלאכה of לש.

keyTerms.meaning: a forceful manner of feeding calves (explained later in the גמרא)

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets the guidelines for feeding animals on שבת, which comes up in practical halacha for anyone caring for animals.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not overfeed the camel
and may not force-feed, but one may place food in its mouth.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַאֲמִירִין אֶת הָעֲגָלִים, אֲבָל מַלְעִיטִין.
phrases.english: And one may not feed the calves by hamra'a, but one may by halata.
And one may force-feed the chickens,
and one may put water into bran,
but one may not knead it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; a new topic begins
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forceful feeding is forbidden, placing food in the mouth is allowed, and bran may be wetted but not kneaded.

steps.title: משנה: giving water to bees, doves, geese, and chickens
steps.stepSummary: One may not put out water for bees or for doves in a dovecote, since they find their own. One may put out water for geese, chickens, and הרדיסיות doves.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not put water before bees or before doves in a dovecote. But one may put water before geese, chickens, and הרדיסיות doves.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second rule, about giving water to different creatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on whether the creature relies on the owner. Bees and dovecote doves get their own food and drink outside, so serving them is needless טרחא. Geese, chickens, and house doves depend on their owner.

phrases.english: And one may not put water before bees
or before doves that are in the dovecote,
but one may put [water] before geese and chickens,
and before hardisian doves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water may be given only to creatures that depend on their owner.

steps.title: What does 'overfeed' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the משנה's term אין אובסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: What is 'one may not overfeed'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה by asking what the word אובסין means. This sets up רב יהודה's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אובסין is an unusual word, so before applying the rule we need to know exactly what action it forbids.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is 'one may not overfeed'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה

steps.title: רב יהודה: making a trough inside its stomach
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that אובסין means stuffing the camel so full that its stomach becomes like a feeding trough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: One may not make a trough for it inside its stomach.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה defines the forbidden act. It means feeding the camel a huge amount at once, so food is stored inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אובסין is linked to אבוס, a trough. The camel is stuffed so much that its belly holds food like a trough does.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹשִׂין לָהּ אֵבוּס בְּתוֹךְ מֵעֶיהָ.
phrases.english: One may not make a trough for it inside its stomach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: אֵין עוֹשִׂין לָהּ אֵבוּס בְּתוֹךְ מֵעֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אובסין means stuffing the camel until its stomach becomes like a trough.

steps.title: Can a camel really be fed that much?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether it is actually possible to stuff a camel like that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there such a thing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether רב יהודה's definition matches reality. This sets up a story as the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A definition must describe something that can really happen. The גמרא wonders whether any animal could hold such a huge amount of food.

phrases.english: Is there [anything] like this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the realism of step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a camel can actually be stuffed to that degree

steps.title: רב ירמיה מדיפתי saw a camel fed a כור and loaded with a כור
steps.stepSummary: Yes. רב ירמיה מדיפתי reports seeing an Arab who fed his camel a כור of food and then loaded another כור onto its back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as רב ירמיה of דיפתי said: I myself saw an Arab who fed it a כור and loaded it with a כור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא confirms with an eyewitness report that a camel really can be stuffed with a huge amount of food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Arab fed the camel a כור, a very large measure. The camel then carried that food inside its belly and another כור on its back. This shows that the trough-in-the-stomach case is real, which is why the משנה needed to forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: a כור, a very large dry measure

steps.whatToRemember: אין אובסין means not stuffing a camel until its belly holds food like a trough. This really happens, as רב ירמיה מדיפתי saw.

phrases.english: Yes, and as Rav Yirmeya of Difti said:
I myself saw a certain Arab
who fed it a kor and loaded it with a kor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 with an eyewitness report
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. A camel was seen fed a כור and loaded with a כור.

steps.title: What Is the Difference Between הַמְרָאָה and הַלְעָטָה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'אין מאמירין' and asks how הַמְרָאָה (forbidden) differs from הַלְעָטָה (permitted).
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may not do הַמְרָאָה.' Which feeding counts as הַמְרָאָה, and which counts as הַלְעָטָה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up a new phrase from the משנה and asks what its two feeding terms mean. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids הַמְרָאָה on שבת but allows הַלְעָטָה. Both mean putting food into an animal's mouth, so we need to know exactly where the line falls between them.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not do הַמְרָאָה (a forbidden way of stuffing food into an animal)
A type of force-feeding that is forbidden on שבת
A gentler type of feeding into the mouth that is permitted on שבת

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] One may not do hamra'ah.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, which introduces the new discussion.

phrases.english: Which is hamra'ah,
and which is hal'atah?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזוֹ הִיא הַמְרָאָה וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא הַלְעָטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the explanation of אובסין to the next term in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact definitions of הַמְרָאָה and הַלְעָטָה and what separates them.

steps.title: רב יהודה: It Depends on How Deep the Food Goes
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says הַמְרָאָה puts food deep into the throat, where the animal cannot bring it back up. הַלְעָטָה puts it where the animal can still spit it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: הַמְרָאָה means putting food so deep that the animal cannot bring it back up. הַלְעָטָה means putting it in a place where the animal can still bring it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the first definition. For him, the difference is how deep the food is placed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pushing food deep into the throat forces the animal to swallow it, so it is more like real work and is forbidden. Leaving it where the animal can still reject it is lighter, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring back up or spit out
Into a place (here, a spot in the mouth or throat)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Hamra'ah is putting food into a place from which it cannot bring it back,
hal'atah is putting it into a place from which it can bring it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is depth. Deep placement that cannot be undone is הַמְרָאָה. Shallow placement that can be undone is הַלְעָטָה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: It Depends on Tool Versus Hand
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says both kinds of feeding put food deep in the throat. הַמְרָאָה uses a tool, and הַלְעָטָה is done by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: In both cases the food goes where the animal cannot bring it back. The difference is that הַמְרָאָה is done with a tool, and הַלְעָטָה is done by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a different definition. For him, the difference is the method of feeding, not the depth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב חסדא, even deep feeding is allowed if it is done by hand. Only using a tool makes it the forbidden הַמְרָאָה. This sets up a clear argument with רב יהודה, which the next steps will test.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

steps.confusionAlert: For רב חסדא, הַלְעָטָה is also deep feeding. The only difference is tool versus hand. Do not mix this up with רב יהודה's depth-based definition.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי לִמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לְהַחֲזִיר,
phrases.english: Both this and that are into a place from which it cannot bring it back,
but hamra'ah is with a tool,
and hal'atah is by hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יהודה's definition in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both go deep. A tool makes it הַמְרָאָה, and a hand makes it הַלְעָטָה.

steps.title: רב יוסף Quotes a Teaching About Chickens and Doves
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא: one may do מהלקטין for chickens, and certainly מלקיטין. For dovecote and attic doves, one may not even do מלקיטין, and certainly not מהלקטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected from a teaching: One may do 'מהלקטין' for chickens, and of course 'מלקיטין' too. For doves in a dovecote or an attic, one may not do 'מלקיטין', and of course not 'מהלקטין'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף opens a challenge by quoting a ברייתא. He has not yet explained the problem. This step sets up the analysis that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses two feeding words. מהלקטין is the stronger one and מלקיטין is the lighter one. The challenge will depend on what these words mean.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection from a source
A stronger kind of feeding (its meaning is about to be debated)
A lighter kind of feeding (its meaning is about to be debated)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
One may do mehalketin for chickens,
and needless to say, one may do malkitin.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַלְקִיטִין לְיוֹנֵי שׁוֹבָךְ וּלְיוֹנֵי עֲלִיָּיה,
phrases.english: And one may not do malkitin for dovecote doves or attic doves,
and needless to say, one may not do mehalketin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to test the dispute between רב יהודה and רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The attack is only set up here. It will be built in steps 17 to 19 by working out the meaning of the ברייתא's terms.

steps.title: What Do the Two Feeding Words Mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what מהלקטין and מלקיטין mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'מהלקטין' and what is 'מלקיטין'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to define the ברייתא's two words. This prepares the reading that will become the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on these definitions. If they turn out to be about depth, the ברייתא can be compared to the משנה's הַמְרָאָה and הַלְעָטָה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? What does it mean?

phrases.english: What is 'mehalketin' and what is 'malkitin'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the words of the ברייתא quoted in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definitions of מהלקטין and מלקיטין.

steps.title: The Hand-Versus-Throwing Reading Seems Impossible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that מהלקטין means feeding by hand and מלקיטין means throwing food in front of the birds. It rejects this, because then even throwing food before doves would be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that 'מהלקטין' means feeding the bird by hand and 'מלקיטין' means throwing food in front of them, then it would follow that you may not even throw food in front of dovecote and attic doves. Can that be?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible meaning and pushes it aside because it leads to a strange result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, the ברייתא would forbid simply tossing food in front of doves. That seems too strict, since throwing food is the easiest possible kind of feeding. So the גמרא looks for a different meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
That he feeds it with his hand
That he throws it in front of them

phrases.english: If you say mehalketin means that he feeds it with his hand,
and malkitin means that he throws it in front of them,
it would follow that for dovecote doves and attic doves
even throwing food in front of them is not allowed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries one answer to the question of step 17 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading of מהלקטין as hand-feeding and מלקיטין as throwing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would forbid even throwing food before doves, which seems unreasonable.

steps.title: The Depth Reading Refutes רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: So the words must be about depth: מהלקטין is deep feeding, and מלקיטין is shallow. Since the ברייתא allows deep feeding for chickens, the forbidden הַמְרָאָה must be feeding with a tool. That refutes רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it that 'מהלקטין' means putting food where the bird cannot bring it back, and 'מלקיטין' means putting it where it can? Then it follows that הַמְרָאָה is with a tool, and this is a refutation of רב יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now finishes רב יוסף's challenge. It reads the ברייתא as being about depth and shows that this contradicts רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows deep feeding for chickens. רב יהודה said deep feeding is the forbidden הַמְרָאָה. So the forbidden kind must be something else, namely using a tool, which is רב חסדא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it that (introduces the preferred reading)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו, מְהַלְקְטִין — לִמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לְהַחֲזִיר,
phrases.english: Rather, isn't it that mehalketin is into a place from which it cannot bring it back,
and malkitin is into a place from which it can bring it back?
It follows that hamra'ah is with a tool,
and this is a refutation of Rav Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו מְהַלְקְטִין לִמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לְהַחֲזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of step 18 and completes the attack begun in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's view that deep feeding is the forbidden הַמְרָאָה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows deep feeding for chickens. So deep feeding cannot be what the משנה forbids. The forbidden kind must be feeding with a tool, which is רב חסדא's view.

steps.title: רב יהודה: Doves Are Not Your Responsibility
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה keeps the hand-versus-throwing reading. He explains that even throwing food before doves is forbidden, because feeding them is not your responsibility, unlike chickens.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה can answer you: In truth, 'מהלקטין' means feeding by hand, and 'מלקיטין' means throwing food in front of them. And what bothered you, that you may not even throw food in front of doves? Those chickens are your responsibility to feed, but these doves are not your responsibility to feed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה defends himself. He goes back to the reading that was rejected and shows it is not strange after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Chickens depend on their owner for food, so feeding them on שבת is allowed. Doves can find their own food, so the owner has no duty to feed them. Even tossing food to them is extra effort that is not allowed on שבת. Now the ברייתא is not about depth, and רב יהודה's definition survives.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)
Actually, really (going back to an earlier reading)

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה survives the challenge. The ברייתא is about hand versus throwing, and doves are different because their food is not your responsibility.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda can say to you:
Actually, 'mehalketin' means that he feeds it by hand,
and 'malkitin' means that he throws it in front of them.
And as for what bothered you,
that for dovecote doves and attic doves
even throwing food in front of them is not allowed?
These [chickens] are your responsibility to feed,
and these [doves] are not your responsibility to feed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation in step 19 by bringing back the reading rejected in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the source plus a new distinction (whose food is your responsibility)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forbidding even throwing food before doves seemed absurd, so the ברייתא had to be about depth.
steps.terutzMaskana: Throwing food before doves really is forbidden, because their food is not your responsibility. So the ברייתא is about hand versus throwing, and רב יהודה stands.

steps.title: Support from the Dog and the Pig
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says you may put food before a dog on שבת but not before a pig, because a dog's food is your responsibility and a pig's is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: You may put food in front of a dog, but you may not put food in front of a pig. What is the difference between them? This one's food is your responsibility, and that one's food is not your responsibility.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רב יהודה's distinction from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the exact idea of whose food is your responsibility to permit feeding one animal and forbid another. Dogs are commonly kept, but a Jew does not raise pigs. This shows the distinction is a known rule, not something invented just to answer the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a lasting rule of feeding animals on שבת: you may feed animals that depend on you, but not ones you have no duty to feed.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
One may put food in front of a dog,
but one may not put food in front of a pig.
And what is the difference between this and that?
This one's food is your responsibility,
and that one's food is not your responsibility.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the distinction רב יהודה used in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that you may only feed animals whose food is your responsibility on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a dog and a pig

steps.title: רב אשי brings support from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says our משנה also shows that the key factor is whether the animal's food is your responsibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Our משנה is also precise this way. It says you may not put water before bees or before doves in a dovecote, but you may put water before geese, chickens, and hardisian doves. What is the reason? Is it not because the food of these animals is your responsibility, and the food of those animals is not?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a proof for רב יהודה's idea from the wording of our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets you give water to geese and chickens but not to bees and wild doves. רב אשי says the only difference between these groups is whether you are responsible for feeding them. That matches רב יהודה's rule from the previous steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה is also precise, meaning its wording supports this idea
Dovecote, where wild doves nest and fly out to find their own food
Hardisian doves, house-raised doves that depend on their owner

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Our Mishnah is also precise in this way,
one may not place water
before bees or before doves in a dovecote,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נוֹתְנִין לִפְנֵי אֲווֹזִין וְלִפְנֵי תַרְנְגוֹלִין
phrases.english: but one may place it before geese and before chickens
and before hardisian doves.
What is the reason?
Is it not because these, their food is your responsibility,
and those, their food is not your responsibility?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof, this time from the משנה, after the ברייתא about the dog and the pig.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's rule that feeding on שבת depends on whether the animal's food is your responsibility
steps.raayaSupportSource: The precise wording of our משנה, which separates bees and dovecote doves from geese, chickens, and hardisian doves

steps.title: Why would the משנה mention only water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי: if responsibility were the reason, the משנה should forbid even grain, not just water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, why does the משנה mention water specifically? Even wheat and barley should also not be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's proof by asking why the משנה singles out water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule were about responsibility, any food would be forbidden for bees and wild doves. Yet the משנה talks only about water. That suggests a different reason, one that is specific to water.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning, which sets up a problem with the other side's logic

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
why does it mention water specifically?
Even wheat and barley should also not be allowed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof רב אשי just brought.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reading of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A responsibility-based rule would cover all food. The משנה's focus on water shows the reason must be something about water itself.

steps.title: Water is different because it is found in lakes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the משנה differently: water is special because animals can easily find it in lakes, so the proof falls away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, water is different, because it is commonly found in a lake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real reason for the משנה's rule, which removes רב אשי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bees and wild doves can easily drink from a lake, so there is no need to bother bringing them water on שבת. This reason applies only to water and has nothing to do with responsibility. So the משנה does not prove רב יהודה's point.
steps.confusionAlert: This step rejects only רב אשי's proof from the משנה. It does not reject רב יהודה's rule, which still stands on the ברייתא of the dog and the pig.

phrases.english: Rather, water is different,
because it is commonly found in a lake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 with a water-specific reason, ending רב אשי's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה is rejected, not רב יהודה's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's distinction can be explained by water being easy to find, not by responsibility for feeding.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's proof from the משנה falls away because water is easy to find in lakes. רב יהודה's rule still rests on the ברייתא of the dog and the pig.

steps.title: ה׳ cares for the dog, whose food is scarce
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה explains a פסוק to mean that ה׳ knows a dog is rarely fed, so its food stays in its stomach for three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונה expounded at the entrance of the house of the נשיא: What is meant by the פסוק 'The righteous one knows the cause of the poor'? הקדוש ברוך הוא knows that a dog's food is scarce. Therefore its food stays in its stomach for three days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shifts to the dog, the animal from the ברייתא, and brings a teaching about ה׳'s care for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונה reads 'the righteous one' in the פסוק as הקדוש ברוך הוא, and 'the poor' as the dog, which people barely feed. ה׳'s answer is that a dog digests slowly, so a little food lasts it a long time.

keyTerms.meaning: At the entrance of the house of the נשיא
The righteous one knows the cause of the poor (משלי כט:ז)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yona expounded
at the entrance of the house of the Nasi:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'The righteous one knows the cause of the poor'?
The Holy One, Blessed be He, knows about the dog
that its food is scarce;

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ שׁוֹהָה אֲכִילָתוֹ בְּמֵעָיו שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים.
phrases.english: therefore its food remains in its stomach for three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַשׁ רַבִּי יוֹנָה אַפִּיתְחָא דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the dog from the ברייתא in step 21 and opens an אגדה section about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ made a dog's food stay in its stomach three days because the dog is rarely fed.

steps.title: A משנה confirms the dog's three-day digestion
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about טומאה confirms that food stays in a dog's stomach for three full days, unlike birds and fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: How long does an animal's food stay in its stomach and remain impure? For a dog, three days of twenty-four hours each. For birds and fish, as long as it takes for the food to fall into a fire and be burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי יונה's claim about dogs with a משנה from the laws of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה deals with an animal that ate impure food, such as flesh from a dead body, and asks how long that food stays undigested and still impure. For a dog the answer is three full days. For birds and fish it is a very short time, which proves the dog digests unusually slowly.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
How long does its food remain in its stomach
and stay impure?
For a dog, three days of full twenty-four hour periods;
and for birds and fish,
as long as it takes to fall into a fire and be burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the factual claim at the heart of רבי יונה's teaching.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יונה's claim that a dog's food stays in its stomach three days
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה in the laws of טומאה about how long swallowed food stays undigested

steps.title: It is proper to throw a dog some meat
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא learns from רבי יונה's teaching that it is good manners to throw a piece of meat to a dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: Learn from this that it is proper conduct to throw a piece of meat to a dog.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא draws a practical lesson from the teaching about the dog.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ה׳ Himself cares that the dog is poorly fed, people should copy that care. So רב המנונא calls feeding a dog a matter of דרך ארץ, proper behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: Proper conduct, the decent way to behave

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:
Learn from it that it is proper conduct
to throw a piece of meat to a dog.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical lesson from רבי יונה's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is proper conduct to throw a piece of meat to a dog.

steps.title: How much should one give a dog?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much meat one should throw to a dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the amount, which sets up רב מרי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא said to feed a dog but did not say how much. This short question asks for that detail.

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the amount in רב המנונא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount of meat one should throw to a dog

steps.title: The size of its ear, then a stick
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי says to give a piece the size of the dog's ear and then follow it with a stick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: The size of its ear, and a stick after it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי answers how much to give a dog.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The piece should be about the size of the dog's ear, a small amount. Afterward you chase it off with a stick so the dog does not become attached to you and keep following you.

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
The size of its ear,
and a stick after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A piece the size of the dog's ear, followed by chasing it away with a stick.

steps.title: Only in the field, not in the city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the practice to the open field. In the city you should not feed a dog, because it will follow you.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies in the field. But in the city, no, because the dog will come to follow him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the practice of feeding a dog.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the open field, a stray dog has few people to feed it, and it is easy to send away. In the city, a dog that gets fed will be drawn to keep following you, so you should not feed it there.

keyTerms.meaning: To be drawn after, to follow along

phrases.english: These words apply in the field,
but in the city, no,
because it will come to follow him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּדַבְרָא, אֲבָל בְּמָתָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows where the feeding practice applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throw a dog meat only in the field, not in the city, because there it will follow you.

steps.title: Nothing poorer than a dog, nothing richer than a pig
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא closes the section: no creature is poorer than a dog, and none is richer than a pig.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: There is none poorer than a dog, and none richer than a pig.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא sums up the contrast between the dog and the pig that ran through this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dog gets very little food, while a pig eats anything and people feed it plenty. This ties back to the ברייתא about putting food before a dog but not a pig on שבת, and to the idea that ה׳ cares for the poor dog.
steps.whatToRemember: The dog is the 'poor' animal: its food is scarce, so ה׳ made it digest slowly, and it is proper to feed it. The pig is the 'rich' animal and needs no special care. This matches the ברייתא that you may feed a dog on שבת but not a pig.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
There is none poorer than a dog,
and there is none richer than a pig.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the dog section with a summary saying that contrasts the dog with the pig.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dog is the poorest creature and the pig the richest, which explains both ה׳'s special care for the dog and the ברייתא's different rules for the two animals.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines המראה and הלעטה in line with רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב יהודה. It defines המראה as forced feeding and הלעטה as feeding the animal in its normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in line with רב יהודה: What is המראה and what is הלעטה? המראה means laying the animal down, forcing its mouth open, and feeding it vetch and water at the same time. הלעטה means feeding the animal and giving it drink while it stands, giving the vetch on its own and the water on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב יהודה by explaining the two feeding methods mentioned in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: המראה is forceful: the animal is pinned down, its mouth is held open, and food and water go in together so it cannot spit them out. הלעטה is gentle: the animal stands normally, and food and drink are given separately, so it can still reject them. This matches רב יהודה's line between food the animal cannot bring back and food it can. The ברייתא says nothing about using a tool versus a hand, which is רב חסדא's line.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that supports his view
Forced feeding, with the animal lying down and its mouth held open
Feeding while the animal stands normally, giving food and water separately
Vetch, a type of animal feed

phrases.english: A baraita was taught in accordance with Rav Yehuda:
What is hamra'ah,
and what is halata?
Hamra'ah: he lays it down and forces its mouth open
and feeds it vetch and water at the same time.
phrases.notes: So the animal cannot spit it out

phrases.english: Halata: he feeds it while it is standing
and gives it drink while it is standing,
and one gives the vetch by itself
and the water by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side discussion about dogs and pigs to the משנה's feeding terms, and supports רב יהודה
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's explanation of the feeding terms in the משנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא defining המראה and הלעטה

steps.title: אביי asks whose view the משנה follows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about feeding chickens and adding water to bran. אביי reports that he asked his teacher whose opinion this משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may force-feed chickens, etc.' אביי said: I said this before my Master: Whose opinion is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, which allows putting water into bran but not kneading it. אביי asks which תנא holds this view, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: one may put water into bran but may not knead it. The question is which תנא holds that adding water by itself is not kneading. אביי's 'Master' is his teacher רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Force-feeding (chickens) by placing food in their mouths
I said it before my Master (רבה)

phrases.english: 'One may force-feed chickens, etc.'
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה. The 'etc.' includes adding water to bran without kneading

phrases.english: Abaye said:
I said it before my Master:
Whose opinion is our Mishnah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic on the next line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that one may put water into bran on שבת as long as one does not knead it

steps.title: רבה answers that it follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the משנה follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה. In a ברייתא, he holds that one is liable for kneading only when one actually kneads, not just for adding water.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: It is רבי יוסי בר יהודה, as it was taught: If one person puts in flour and another puts water into it, the second one is liable. These are the words of רבי. רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: One is not liable until he kneads.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי's question. The משנה follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה, and he proves this from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, pouring water onto flour already counts as the מלאכה of kneading. According to רבי יוסי בר יהודה, the מלאכה only happens when one actually mixes. The משנה allows adding water to bran but forbids kneading it, which matches רבי יוסי בר יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: The last one (who adds the water) is liable

phrases.english: And he said to me:
It is Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda.
As it was taught in a baraita:
One person places the flour
and another places water into it:
the latter is liable. These are the words of Rebbi.
phrases.notes: Adding water already counts as kneading

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
He is not liable until he kneads.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לִי: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה, who holds that adding water is not yet kneading

steps.title: Maybe bran is different from flour
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוסי בר יהודה may have been lenient only with flour, which can be kneaded. With bran, which cannot really be kneaded, he might agree that adding water alone is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps רבי יוסי בר יהודה only said this there about flour, which is kneadable. But with bran, which is not kneadable, even רבי יוסי בר יהודה agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבה's identification. The ברייתא was about flour, not bran, so it may not prove anything about our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With flour, real kneading is still to come, so adding water might not count yet. Bran never forms a true dough, so adding water may be the whole act, and it might be forbidden even according to רבי יוסי בר יהודה. If so, the משנה would not match him after all.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said his ruling up to this point (in this case)
Kneadable, able to become a dough

phrases.english: Perhaps he only said his ruling
(that is,) Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda, there
about flour, which can be kneaded,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מוּרְסָן דְּלָאו בַּר גִּיבּוּל הוּא,
phrases.english: but bran, which cannot be kneaded,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה מוֹדֶה.
phrases.english: even Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda agrees (that it is forbidden).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 34
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the flour ברייתא, not the identification itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא spoke about flour, and bran may follow a different rule

steps.title: An explicit ברייתא shows he permits water in bran
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the flour/bran distinction. An explicit ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי בר יהודה permits putting water into bran.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be, because it was taught explicitly: One may not put water into bran. These are the words of רבי. רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: One may put water into bran.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the doubt from the last step. Another ברייתא speaks about bran directly and shows רבי יוסי בר יהודה is lenient there too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No guessing is needed, because a source deals with bran itself. רבי forbids adding water to bran, and רבי יוסי בר יהודה permits it. So רבה's identification stands: the משנה follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; that idea is rejected
One may put water into bran

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה that permits adding water to bran but forbids kneading follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה. In his view, the מלאכה of kneading begins with the actual mixing, not with adding the water.

phrases.english: It cannot enter your mind,
for it was taught explicitly:
One may not place water into bran;
these are the words of Rebbi.
Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
One may place water into bran.

steps.title: A dispute about kneading roasted-grain flour
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: one may not knead קלי on שבת, and 'some say' one may.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may not knead קלי (flour of roasted young grain). And some say: One may knead it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a dispute about kneading קלי on שבת. This sets up the next question about who the 'some say' are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קלי is flour made from unripe grain dried in an oven. The first view forbids kneading it, and the 'יש אומרים' permit it. The גמרא will now try to identify the 'יש אומרים'.

keyTerms.meaning: Flour of roasted or oven-dried young grain

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not knead roasted-grain flour.
And some say: One may knead it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין גּוֹבְלִין אֶת הַקָּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on a related kneading topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute over whether one may knead קלי on שבת: forbidden according to the first view, permitted according to the 'יש אומרים'

steps.title: Who are the unnamed 'some say'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the 'יש אומרים' are. רב חסדא begins to answer, and his answer continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is 'some say'? רב חסדא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which named תנא stands behind the anonymous 'יש אומרים'. רב חסדא's answer begins here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא often tries to give a name to an unnamed opinion so it can tie the view to a known approach. Here, the lenient view about kneading קלי needs an author. Only the attribution 'אמר רב חסדא' appears on this amud. The content of his answer comes on the next amud.
steps.confusionAlert: The step ends with 'אמר רב חסדא:' and no answer yet. His answer is in the next section, so do not look for it here.
